newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Insurer urges Asia financial services deregulation.
newsitem.headline: Insurer urges Asia financial services deregulation.

text.p: Deregulating Asia's financial services industry must start now if indigenous insurers are to survive in a liberalised market which will attract the world's most advanced financial institutions, a senior industry figure said on Thursday.

"Countries will have to change their regulatory systems to respond to growing competition -- they will have to deregulate," said Yong-Kil Shin, executive director of Korea's Kyobo Life Insurance Company.

Speaking on the final day of the East Asian Insurance Congress conference in Singapore, Shin told delegates liberalisation could not be reversed and competition from other parts of the globe would have a massive impact on the region's insurers.

"We have to enhance our competitiveness to survive the fierce competition," Shin said. He recommended four key measures: strategic management, new product development, improved sales and efficient asset management.

Shin said deregulating financial services would provide the best form of competitive defence. "By learning how to compete in the free market economy through this effort (deregulation), local financial markets will be able to build up their power to compete with advanced financial institutions."
